category_title: Children with expressive language difficulties and Sotos Syndrome who use persistent, roundabout communication strategies
minimal_context: Maliha is attempting to share her experience of seeing a theatre show with an educator who is busy managing other children in the outdoor play area.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I am going to ride this tricycle around the outdoor play area now.

STUDENT: (Patting the educator's hand) Awa awa awa.

TUTOR: Just a moment, I need to help this other child tie his shoelace first.

STUDENT: (Jumping in joy) This is so much fun... my sister... a dad die. (Bending her body to play the role of 'die')

TUTOR: What are you trying to say? I have to go listen to another child's complaint now.

STUDENT: (Widening her hands to stop the educator's tricycle) Son of lioking... pay ticket... (Claps her hands)

options.A: Provide positive attention to the student when she displays positive behavior, and ignore her when she displays negative behaviors that are harmless.
options.B: Sit down to listen, give time and attention, and ask questions providing options or words for the student to choose from.
options.C: Use a watch timer to prompt a check-in with the student for approximately 30 seconds before each change in routine.
options.D: Remind the student that she is not permitted to use technical language or jargon when communicating in the outdoor play area.
